entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and slightly comic, which takes some of the sting out.
examples: the snoopy neighbor watched us all day

entries.definition: poor enough to need help from others
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Poverty as an affliction that has struck, not a state chosen.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Pretension is built into the gloss - it announces a rank rather than showing one.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Disapproves gently: correct manners held so tightly they have become a fault.

entries.definition: worn and broken down by hard use
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Contemptuous and vivid; it adds squalor to mere wear.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Adds the aftermath: there was no regret once it was done.

entries.definition: having or proceeding from an innately kind disposition
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Innate rather than practised; the kindness precedes the occasion for it.

entries.definition: affecting extreme elegance in dress and manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Beyond dandified: the appearance has crowded out everything else.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *unfeigned*: defined against pretence, which is a curious way to have to say it.
examples: was unfeignedly glad to see his old teacher

entries.definition: with competence; in a competent capable manner
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *apt*: quick to learn - formal and slightly old-fashioned.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *mincing*: mocks refinement as performance - the word describes the walk, and means the person.
examples: she stepped mincingly over the puddles

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *boorish*: ill-manners as a settled character, and contemptible with it.
examples: he behaved boorishly at the party

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *game*: willing to try - courage as good sportsmanship rather than heroism.
examples: he was seen by a shepherd, gamely negotiating a particularly tricky section of the mountain road to San Doloroso

entries.definition: marked by or showing unaffected simplicity and lack of guile or worldly experience
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The everyday word, and gentler than it looks - it blames inexperience, not intellect.
examples: a teenager's naive ignorance of life
the naive assumption that things can only get better

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The everyday accusation, and it is about other people's business specifically.
examples: he flipped through my letters in his nosy way

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Courage defined by what failed to stop it.
examples: undaunted in the face of death

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *courageous*: weightier than 'brave' - implies moral choice, not just nerve.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Reports the feeling without judging it; the mildest and least loaded word in the family.

entries.definition: with much noise or loud and unpleasant sound
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *noisy*: the plain complaint, and a mild one - noise is expected in most places.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Casual and often self-applied - out of money right now.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Mocks the crying as ugly and self-indulgent.
examples: Stop blubbering and tell me what happened.

entries.definition: not pretended; sincerely felt or expressed
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The oldest sense of *true*: loyal and unfeigned, not merely correct.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Harder than *closefisted* by a shade, and rarer.

entries.definition: being of delicate or slender build
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Delicately built - descriptive and mild, with no sting.
examples: watched her slight figure cross the street

entries.definition: having desirable or positive qualities especially those suitable for a thing specified
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain word of approval - broad, safe, and unemphatic.

entries.definition: offensively self-assured or given to exercising usually unwarranted power
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Splits cleanly: a magisterial book is authoritative, a magisterial manner is unbearable.
examples: managed the employees in an aloof magisterial way

entries.definition: marked by deliberate deceptiveness especially by pretending one set of feelings and acting under the influence of another
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Biblical in flavour - it condemns the mouth rather than the man.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The blunt word, and a wounding one of a person.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Institutional and euphemistic - it is what discipline is called in a report.
examples: the teacher's action was corrective rather than instructional

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Modern and slightly therapeutic; it names a personality type.
examples: Saturday's child is loving and giving

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Rare, and pulled between light-of-heart and light-of-foot.
examples: trilling songs with a lightsome heart

entries.definition: polished and well-groomed; showing sophisticated elegance
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Grooming and polish rather than taste; it is about the finish.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Crude insult built from an obscenity - offensive in any setting.

entries.definition: (of persons or their actions) able or disposed to inflict pain or suffering
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: *One fell swoop* - on its own it reads as deliberate archaism.

entries.definition: poor enough to need help from others
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The legal and administrative term for qualifying poverty.

entries.definition: resembling a beast; showing lack of human sensibility
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Coarse rather than violent: it says unrefined more than it says cruel.

entries.definition: without pity; in a merciless manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *unmerciful*: the same judgement in the older negative form, and slightly more formal.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Severe and formal - originally of cruelty, now also of quality.

entries.definition: naive and easily deceived or tricked
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Defines the person by what can be done to them, which is why it stings.

entries.definition: (used of persons and their behavior) not refined; uncouth
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Descriptive and mild - it names an absence rather than an offence.
examples: how can a refined girl be drawn to such an unrefined man?

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warm but modest - better than expected without being remarkable.
examples: I would kill for a decent cup of coffee

entries.definition: soiled or likely to soil with dirt or grime
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Clinical and euphemistic - the word hospitals and laundries use to avoid *dirty*.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *handsome*: praises strong, well-proportioned looks; dignity rather than prettiness.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *grungy*: informal and unimpressed, though a whole music scene wore it as a badge.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Implies force rather than time, and of a person it means something much worse.

entries.definition: of a stern or strict bearing or demeanor; forbidding in aspect
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The face more than the rule; sternness is something the other person can see.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal and warm, and often used of judgement under pressure.
examples: observant and thoughtful, he was given to asking sagacious questions

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same accusation in the plainer word; no part of the person is exempted.
